record.tranche_reason: The paper tests learning-curve power-law behavior in supervised image classification, a different modality and training regime from language-model pretraining. Its own measurements are test error versus training-set size, not language-model held-out cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses language-model scaling work, including Kaplan et al., but those cited findings are not its own results. Its experiments measure test error for binarized image-classification datasets while varying training-set size, and compare those curves with a PAC-Bayes bound. It does not measure parameter-, token-, or compute-scaling, or a compute-optimal allocation.
record.test_reason: The paper's own experiments measure 0-1 test error against training-set size for 19 architectures on 5 binarized image datasets. That gives a direct result on whether power-law data scaling holds in supervised image classification, a regime other than LM pretraining (V5). It also shows exponents shifting with dataset and curve shape shifting with batch size (V7). The PAC-Bayes bound is the paper's own method. Its performance is not a test of the claim, so verdicts rest only on the empirical learning curves.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with two additions. The authors also prove their bound is asymptotically optimal (up to a constant) when learning curves follow a power law. They report that the bound tracks the empirical learning-curve exponents, including the FCN outlier. They note it covers only the data-limited regime (infinite width, trained to zero error), not model-size or compute-optimal scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies training-set size for supervised image classifiers and measures 0-1 test error, using binarized datasets and a PAC-Bayes/NNGP estimate. It does not reproduce language-model pretraining-loss sweeps over parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported curve behavior varies with dataset, architecture, and batch size. The authors also state that fitted exponents can be sensitive to the measurement protocol; the PAC-Bayes exponent estimates are affected by systematic errors from the expectation-propagation approximation.
record.problems: The experimental results are for supervised image-classification test error, not language-model pretraining loss. Most curve results are presented graphically and the text gives few numerical exponents. Some large-training-set points use only one random initialization; the marginal likelihood uses NNGP and expectation-propagation approximations, whose errors are not rigorously guaranteed.
record.rows_left_out: Per-architecture and per-dataset curves in Figures 2-4, 8-17 are not separately extracted; the text's aggregate descriptions are recorded instead. No numerical exponent values are stated in the text. Findings cited from other papers are excluded.

untested.parts: Only data-size scaling of 0-1 test error in binarized supervised image classification. Not tested: parameter or compute scaling, cross-entropy loss, generative image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer.
Not tested: parameter-counting choices, learning-rate schedules, compute-optimal splits, or fitting-method comparisons. The authors only cite sensitivity of exponents to the measurement protocol.
Not tested: language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Not tested: extrapolation from small to large runs.
Architectures are compared, but not at a fixed parameter count. Depth is varied only for a CNN at fixed data, and only the bound-versus-error correlation is reported.

missing.what: Batch-256 exponent comparison: exponents again cluster by dataset, and the FCN is again the outlier for MNIST and KMNIST. This replicates r1 under a second training setting.

record.verdict_notes: Accepted as T3 on V5 because the paper's ground-truth learning curves are its own measurements across many architectures and datasets. However, they measure data-size scaling of 0-1 test error with binarized labels only, and give no numeric exponents in the text. The paper's focus is the bound, so evidence on the claim is secondary and mostly graphical.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits from small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation, including how either grows with compute.
The paper compares architectures, but does not hold parameter count fixed to test whether architectural details change loss only slightly.
The experiments concern supervised binary image classification and test error, not pretraining cross-entropy; they do not test video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Predictability of downstream-task performance from language-model scale or pretraining loss.
The paper does not test language-model scaling exponents, parameter-counting choices, compute-optimal splits, or whether language-model curves bend with model size, tokens, or compute.

rows.subject: 19 architectures (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured empirical test-error learning curves while varying training-set size.

conditions.value: five binarized image datasets: MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, EMNIST, KMNIST, CIFAR10

rows.measure: Empirical test-error learning-curve power-law behavior and fitted exponent
rows.value: The curves generally show power-law behavior; exponents cluster by dataset, with smaller but statistically significant variation among architectures. The fully connected network is an outlier for MNIST and KMNIST.
rows.uncertainty: Estimated standard errors from linear fits are shown; numerical values not stated in the text.
rows.note: Aggregate summary of the authors' image-classification experiments. The fitted empirical exponents use a linear fit of log test error versus log training-set size.
rows.check: For V5 the state should be observed, not partial. The authors say the curves agree with power-law behaviour "with only a few exceptions", and the CIFAR10 batch-32 exception is already row r2. For V7, exponents clustering by dataset, plus smaller but significant architecture variation, is the data-dependence V7 names. The measure is 0-1 test error versus data size only, not cross-entropy, parameters or compute.

rows.subject: CIFAR10 learning curves (aggregate; architectures not specified in the textual statement)
rows.operation_detail: Measured empirical test error as training-set size varied.
rows.measure: Shape of empirical test-error learning curve
rows.value: The learning curve appears to deviate from a power law over the tested range of training-set sizes.
rows.note: The authors contrast this with the cleaner power-law behavior seen for CIFAR10 at batch size 256.
rows.check: For V5 the state is partial: the CIFAR10 batch-32 curve "appears to deviate from a power law on this range of m" (Sec 7.2), though error still falls. For V7 this row is effectively observed: the curve bends away from a single power law under one training setting. The architectures are not named; per Fig 3/4 they include FCN, Resnet50, Densenet121 and MobileNetv2.

relationships.condition: Supervised image classification learning curves (test error vs data size)
